questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: First and foremost due to my interest in Italian culture and architecture. Secondly, the University of Bologna is the oldest in Europe and due to the large number of students in Bologna, the city is also very politically active. I found this intriguing both personally and academically.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: When I first came to Bologna, there was a check-in for exchange students where I spoke to an employee from the university. It was good and informative. However, generally speaking, I will say that the university system, e.g. course schedules, class locations, exam info, has sometimes been lacking and difficult to see through, especially for exchange students who are not assisted very well in this regard.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above, there was a brief phone conversation during the "Check-in". That was mostly about the Learning Agreement, how to fill out you study plan and where to print your university ID-cards (which is good), but not so informative of the day-to-day university life, how to enroll and attend classes etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky and found housing through a contact back home. Generally finding housing in Bologna, especially as an exchange student, is very challenging and expensive. Maybe the KU and UNIBO system could work together to offer a guide/overview of where to look for housing before coming to Bologna.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Well, if you wish to meet new people you have to more actively seek social events since you're not living with other students. But I'd definitely recommend living off campus/not in student apartments.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
As previously mentioned, it was difficult to actually enroll for the courses and getting access to the course resources/schedule/readings etc. Even though my courses where accepted and on my learning agreement, it seemed as if no one knew I was attending them. I didn't receive any information or access to the course's online resources beforehand, which made the beginning a bit uncertain. 

Other than that, the registration process prior to arriving in Bologna was also very time consuming and frustrating. It seemed as if KU and UNIBO's systems didn't work together which caused me a lot of trouble in terms of getting my Learning Agreement accepted and signed. There was no issues with registration (my acceptance to UNIBO) but I wish there would have been a physical/online info meeting provided by the university close to the semester start, that I could have attended before going to Bologna.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: At UNIBO there was an exchange student help desk. I only used their email services, and I'm actually not sure if there is a physical office you can go to.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Late in the process I found out that I had been accepted to the department of Language and Literature, so I had to redo my Learning Agreement because of a demand to take at least one course that is taught at that department.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the "Going abroad" help desks at KU for any questions you might have, and call the host university (if it's possible) if you have any trouble with registering. You can get extremely lost in emails, forms and different platforms, so I would highly recommend human contact when sorting out your exchange.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had the opportunity to take elective MA-courses even though I'm a BA student. So I did both, but a difference in difficulty was not noticeable.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less group work and seminars, more lectures. Bigger focus on historical events and the state of 'real life' and less emphasis on theory. A more relaxed attitude towards exams and, thus, less information about exams. No "studieordning" for the courses as we have at UCPH, meaning less structure and more room for the professor and the students to shape the teaching underway.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Women's Movements Worldwide
Introduction to Italian Culture
Gender Studies
Global Diasporas. Cultures, Identities and Politics.
Semiotics of Conflict

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Global Diasporas and Semiotics of Conflict were both relevant, better-structured classes with really interesting and modern theory.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No costs were unexpected. But living costs in general were higher than I anticipated.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is all kinds of things going on. Different sport teams, student organisations, political activism, readings and seminars (for example I went to a seminar with Judith Butler who visited the university). You just have to seek the events and ask around if there's something you wish to participate in.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Whatever you're into. I really liked the political talks and demos, and some of the free seminars you can attend as a student.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit restaurants (restaurants with traditional food in Bologna is generally cheap and good). Take the train and go on small trips. Get out of the city or seek green spaces to clear your mind.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I would say it's not difficult if you're genuinely interested in understanding and adjusting to the culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The daily rhytm (Siesta from about 13-16).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The socialness and food culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make a budget and try to keep it. Be patient with the university system and have faith that your classes, exams etc. will work out well. Come with an open mindset and seize new opportunities when they occur.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you wish to do the Italian classes that are provided by the university, you must do a language placement test beforehand.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a new culture on a deeper level, making international friends and just living abroad in general.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: University bureaucracy.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
